thread:
maria_support: Hey team — IrisPay is seeing 403 errors on webhook deliveries since our maintenance finished. They say their firewall only allows our old egress IPs and now they're blocked. Can someone confirm if we rotated NATs?

ton y_oncall: Looking. I saw a small NAT pool rebalance in the 02:00 UTC window for the us-west private pool. Ops automation logged a reassignment but should have been in the note. :thinking_face:

ops-bot: Automated event: NAT_POOL_REASSIGNMENT executed by autoscaler at 2026-11-03T02:06:12Z. Affected pool: private-us-west-2. Old egress range: 198.51.100.16/28. New egress range: 198.51.101.32/28.

kyle_neteng: Confirmed — we had to move a handful of VPCs off a saturated host group. The NAT addresses were pulled from the shared pool and new addresses were attached. I can pull the audit logs.

emily_support: Can you paste the customer errors so we can show them?

maria_support: Here's what IrisPay sent: "POST https://hooks.irispay.com/receive 403 Forbidden" and they included a curl trace: 

```
curl -v -X POST https://hooks.irispay.com/receive -d '{"id":"evt_123"}' 
> POST /receive HTTP/1.1
> Host: hooks.irispay.com
> X-Forwarded-For: 198.51.101.35
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
< content-type: text/plain
< content-length: 9
<
Forbidden
```

maria_support: They also said their SRE team has an allowlist only for the old block (198.51.100.16/28).

tony_oncall: That explains it. We should share the new block and offer a temporary workaround (route via our dedicated egress for their org or reattach old IPs if possible). Any chance we can reattach the old range?

kyle_neteng: Old block was garbage-collected and reallocated to infra. We can’t guaranteed pin the exact addresses back. Quick options: 1) Give them the new ranges to allowlist (198.51.101.32/28) + examples of single IPs they may see (198.51.101.33-38). 2) Offer a short-term dedicated egress IP (static NAT) — requires provisioning but doable within ~2 hours if accepted.

emily_support: I'll draft the customer message. Maria, can you confirm if they accept the dedicated IP offer? If not, we'll ask them to add the new block. Also open a support ticket with priority high.

maria_support: Yep filing ticket now (#SUP-2026-811). Reached out: asked if they want the dedicated static egress. Waiting on reply. :mailbox_with_mail:

sean_platform: Internal follow-up: we should update the runbook to surface which customers are using shared NAT and have allowlists. Also we need a pre-maintenance notification step listing potential egress IP changes. I'll take the postmortem.

kyle_neteng: For troubleshooting, FYI commands we ran: 
```
# show pool assignment
opsctl nat show --pool private-us-west-2 --json | jq '.assignments | .[] | {vpc, old_ip, new_ip}'
# quick egress check from ephemeral host
ssh runner@ephemeral-node -- curl -s https://ifconfig.co
```
These produced the mapping and the observed outbound IPs.

maria_support: Customer replied: they can add the new /28 for now but want the dedicated option for production traffic. Asking for a quote and SLA.

emily_support: Ok wrote back with the new block (198.51.101.32/28) and offered dedicated egress + timeline. Also shared a short mitigation: set webhook receivers to accept X-Request-ID and verify payloads so retries survive transient 403s.

tony_oncall: I've tagged this incident as "egress-allowlist-drift" and scheduled a brief post-maintenance check to run egress verification for high-risk customers. :white_check_mark:

sean_platform: I'll add a one-liner to the changelog/email template: "If you use IP allowlisting, expect possible egress IP changes for shared NAT pools during maintenance; contact support to request static egress."

maria_support: Ticket updated with new block and the dedicated egress quote placeholder. Will keep thread updated once IrisPay accepts.

emily_support: Thank you — please paste final confirmation here when IrisPay updates their allowlist so we can close.

kyle_neteng: Note for ops: consider adding an opt-in preservation flag for high-risk VPCs to keep old NAT addresses during short rebalances. Filing follow-up RFC.

maria_support: IrisPay confirmed they added 198.51.101.32/28 and webhooks resumed. They accepted a quote request for dedicated egress; will loop in procurement. Closing interim work. :thumbsup:

emily_support: Great — closing ticket in 24h if no regressions. Thanks all.
